transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 14:00 PT | Duration: 75m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Lee (Redwood SE), Rajiv Bhatt (Redwood Perf), Helena Cruz (Redwood), Carlos Mendez (Atlas CTO), Priya Shah (Atlas SRE), Liam O'Connor (Atlas ML), Sophie Keller (Atlas Product)

00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll kick off, quick agenda — align on benchmark methodology, agree on prompt sets, and how we do apples-to-apples loadgen for on-prem vs hosted.
00:21 - Carlos Mendez: Great, thanks. We're particularly sensitive to p99 latency and how KV cache warmup changes numbers. We've seen wide variance when we move from short sequences to long convo history.
00:38 - Jonah Lee: totally. The big traps are different seq length distributions, different batching policies, and not warming the KV cache. We'll walk through a reproducible pipeline.
01:05 - Priya Shah: quick note — network egress in our on-prem will be limited, and we'll want to run within our VPC with a sim of cross-AZ latencies.
01:22 - Maya Patel: noted. We'll include network topology options in the runbook.
01:40 - Rajiv Bhatt: For apples-to-apples, we recommend starting with three canonical profiles: short-chat (~32 tokens), medium-assist (~256 tokens), and long-context (~4k-8k tokens) with a mix of prefix/prompt lengths to mimic your usage. Also plan cold-starts vs warm-cache.
02:10 - Carlos Mendez: How do you recommend we ensemble prompt sets? We have templates, but we want variety and edge cases.
02:28 - Helena Cruz: we'll share a canonical prompt set file. It includes templated prompts, few-shot variants, and adversarial examples. The idea is to have deterministic prompts so token counts are stable.
02:46 - Liam O'Connor: are we going to include function-calling style prompts? That changes output lengths unpredictably.
03:02 - Jonah Lee: include a separate subset with function-calling patterns; mark them as variable-output. For apples-to-apples, separate the fixed-output workloads from variable-output ones.
03:22 - Sophie Keller: timeline question — we need baseline numbers to make an architecture decision in August.
03:35 - Maya Patel: ok so we should prioritize a quick hosted vs on-prem baseline this month, then run more extensive mixed workloads in August.
04:02 - (brief cross-talk)
04:40 - Priya Shah: on load generation — we use Taurus internally but can run Locust/Gatling. What do you prefer?
04:55 - Jonah Lee: we typically provide both templates; Taurus + JMeter for simple replay, and a Gatling script for high throughput. We'll also include warmup orchestration to prefill the KV cache.
05:20 - Carlos Mendez: What about warmup length? We've seen differences where a 5-minute warmup isn't enough for KV to hit steady state.
05:38 - Rajiv Bhatt: depends on workload and model size. Recommend measuring cache hit rate over time and using that to determine warmup. Start with a staged warmup: 15m with the same seq length distribution as your production traces, then a 5m stabilization window.
06:05 - Liam O'Connor: ok that makes sense. We'll need the script to record per-request cache hit/miss so we can correlate latency spikes.
06:20 - Jonah Lee: we'll add KV hit/miss counters to the trace hooks.
06:40 - Maya Patel: quantization — we should calibrate quality vs throughput. Thoughts on supervision and evals?
06:55 - Rajiv Bhatt: make a small eval suite from your most important prompts. Run 8-bit, 4-bit (if supported), and int8/quantized kernels. Compare latency/throughput and run an n-gram and semantic similarity check for regression. We'll also flag hallucination rates for the variable-output set.
07:33 - Carlos Mendez: any gotchas for private/on-prem vs hosted? We worry about kernel differences, OS libraries, and GPU driver versions changing perf.
07:50 - Jonah Lee: exactly — you'll want to snapshot GPU driver, CUDA, cuDNN, libc versions, and include that in the run metadata. For apples-to-apples, match the same kernel builds or use Redwood's reproducible container images for the baseline.
08:20 - Priya Shah: how do we measure per-token cost comparably? Cloud tokens cost model vs on-prem TCO is a bit different.
08:35 - Maya Patel: we provide a per-token unitization model that maps on-prem costs to equivalent $/1k tokens. Rajiv will draft a cost model table.
09:00 - Helena Cruz: important: measure open vs closed loops — i.e., interactive chat (low token per request, many short requests) vs batch generation (fewer requests, large outputs). Batching policies should be tuned differently.
09:30 - (laughter)
09:45 - Liam O'Connor: any guidance on target latencies we should aim for at p95/p99?
10:00 - Rajiv Bhatt: depends on UX. For chat-like, target P95 < 300ms for short responses, p99 < 800ms. For assist with 256 tokens, p95 < 1s is reasonable. For long context 4k+, expect p95 in multiple seconds depending on hardware. We'll document expected ranges per profile.
10:40 - Carlos Mendez: KV cache behavior: do you recommend prefix caching or full KV snapshots for long convos?
10:56 - Jonah Lee: prefix caching (per-session prefix + KV) is typically best; full KV snapshots blow memory and are slower to populate. Also measure GC/eviction policies and how they affect p99 backpressure.
11:25 - Priya Shah: we have regulatory constraints; we need to ensure no PII leaves our VPC during benchmarks. How to simulate real traffic without exfil?
11:40 - Maya Patel: redact sensitive fields in prompt sets; we can provide a redaction script. For on-prem we can also run the whole suite in air-gapped mode.
12:00 - (pause)
12:20 - Carlos Mendez: what's the recommended measurement cadence for latency buckets? 1ms bins?
12:35 - Rajiv Bhatt: 5–10ms bins for short-latency workloads, 50ms bins for larger outputs, and histogram summaries to compute p50/p95/p99. Also include percentiles for tokens/sec throughput.
13:05 - Liam O'Connor: are we going to include warm/cold disk effects? NVMe vs network attached?
13:20 - Jonah Lee: yes include disk tiering as a parameter. For caching it's mostly in GPU memory and host DRAM; but checkpoint loading and model swap can show up in cold-starts. We'll test cold-start model load times separately.
13:45 - Helena Cruz: we'll attach a template results spreadsheet so columns map to metadata like container image, driver version, quantization, batch size, seq len distribution, warmup time, cache hit rate, p95/p99, tokens/s, and cost/unit.
14:10 - Carlos Mendez: apples-to-apples often breaks down on batching — different runtimes have different default batch windows. Thoughts on enforced batching parameters?
14:25 - Rajiv Bhatt: force a fixed batch window and a max batch size across engines during the test. Also try adaptive batching and measure latency tail. Document scheduling jitter.
14:50 - Priya Shah: any benchmark for KV eviction behavior under pressure? We saw evictions causing tail latency in the past.
15:05 - Jonah Lee: we'll include high-concurrency stress test where we intentionally oversubscribe and measure eviction rate and p99 impact. Also capture telemetry for re-queue/backpressure in the serving runtime.
15:40 - Sophie Keller: in terms of artifacts, what will you share?
15:55 - Maya Patel: canonical deck, prompt sets, loadgen configs (Taurus/Gatling), warmup scripts, runbook with network/VPC checklists, and a results template.
16:10 - Carlos Mendez: security review — we'll need SOC2 summary and key management docs before any private deployment runs.
16:25 - Maya Patel: yes we'll attach our SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes.
16:40 - (short silence)
17:10 - Liam O'Connor: on the topic of quantization, do you recommend performing instruction-tuned calibration on our prompt set?
17:28 - Rajiv Bhatt: yes run a calibration pass with your eval suite to tune per-layer quantization where possible. That reduces regression risk. We'll share scripts to do that.
17:58 - Priya Shah: can we see an example of the run metadata format now?
18:12 - Helena Cruz: (shares link in chat) - "https://redwood-internal.example/decks/benchmark-methodology" — that has the CSV schema and the prompt set examples.
18:30 - Carlos Mendez: perfect. For the on-prem run, we'll schedule engineers and get cluster snapshots ready.
18:45 - Maya Patel: action recap — Jonah will share loadgen, Rajiv cost matrix and perf knobs, Helena prompt sets and deck, Maya will send SOC2/KMS summary.
19:05 - (background noise, brief crosstalk)
19:40 - Priya Shah: one more — how do you avoid measurement noise from noisy neighbors on shared infra?
19:58 - Jonah Lee: pin CPUs/GPU to test containers, isolate NICs if possible, and run multiple repeats at different times. Use the median of multiple runs plus bootstrap confidence intervals.
20:30 - Carlos Mendez: good. We'll try to replicate Redwood's dedicated config first.
21:00 - Maya Patel: ok we'll schedule the first hosted baseline next week and an on-prem baseline the week after.
21:20 - (closing)
21:45 - Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and next steps.
22:00 - meeting ended

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mis-hearings ("KV cash" on one line in rough transcript), some proper names garbled; speaker labels auto-assigned then corrected by AE.
